entities.summary:
Aelianus Tacticus, a Greek military writer, lived in Rome during the 2nd century CE. He penned several works on tactics, including 'Tactica' and 'On the Expedition of Alexander', which offered insights into Roman military strategy and the campaigns of Alexander the Great. Aelian's writings had a lasting impact on the development of Western military thought, influencing prominent thinkers such as Vegetius and Julius Caesar. His works also provide valuable information on the Roman Empire's military organization, equipment, and tactics during the Late Antique period.

Aelianus Tacticus was born into a wealthy family and received a classical education in Athens before moving to Rome. He likely served in the Roman military, which gave him firsthand experience with military tactics and strategies. His writings reflect his expertise and provide a unique window into the military culture of the Roman Empire.

Aelianus Tacticus' legacy extends beyond his written works, as his ideas and strategies were incorporated into the Roman military's standard practices. His influence can be seen in the development of the Roman legion and the use of tactics such as the testudo (tortoise) formation. Aelianus Tacticus' writings also provide valuable insights into the cultural and social context of the Roman Empire, shedding light on the lives of Roman soldiers and officers.

In conclusion, Aelianus Tacticus was a significant figure in the history of Western military thought, whose writings had a lasting impact on the development of military strategy and tactics. His legacy continues to be felt in modern military doctrine and practice.
